message.content:
The paramagnetic orbital coupling for a magnetic field along \(Oz\) is

\[
\langle H\rangle \sim \mu_B B m
\]

with

\[
\mu_B = 5.79\times 10^{-5}\ \text{eV/T}.
\]

For \(B=1\ \text{T}\) and small \(m\sim 1\),

\[
\langle H\rangle \sim 5.79\times 10^{-5}\ \text{eV}.
\]

The transition energy corresponding to \(\lambda = 0.4861\ \mu\text{m}\) is

\[
\Delta E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}
\approx \frac{1240\ \text{eV nm}}{486.1\ \text{nm}}
\approx 2.55\ \text{eV}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\frac{\langle H\rangle}{\Delta E}
\sim \frac{5.79\times 10^{-5}}{2.55}
\sim 2.3\times 10^{-5},
\]

so the paramagnetic coupling energy is much smaller than the transition energy.

Answer: B
